crossZoneRenderEnvelope.note: Values recorded across two independent real-browser sessions (Claude in Chrome, real foreground Chrome tab) via window.__drift3dRender (Three.js gl.info). Each zone's own screenshot was visually reviewed live in-session and confirmed to show the correct, distinct rendered scene — see runtime-evidence.md for per-scene confirmation notes. No exact value was invented for a zone not directly observed.

interpretation.statement: No separate reliable desktop FPS figure was obtained because automated background-tab throttling invalidated requestAnimationFrame sampling. The real foreground mobile sample reached 50.5 fps at DPR 3, while all measured desktop scenes remained within the same bounded render-cost envelope (139-175 draw calls, 178644-198124 triangles), both well under the 300 draw-call / 1.5M triangle ceiling. This is treated as an inference that the runtime holds a large margin against its geometric budgets across the four measured zones, not as a proven per-zone desktop fps figure.

deviations: devicePixelRatio observed as 2.0, not the requested 3 — no tool available to force DPR override
touch emulation was not applied — no tool available for Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled
no mobile-width screenshot PNG was produced — see limitations

limitations.description: The `computer` tool's save_to_disk option was tested for all captured scenes and both fallback triggers. It reliably wrote a file, but every file produced — across this session and multiple unrelated historical sessions on this machine — was byte-identical (2,792,674 bytes, 4800x2160px), i.e. an unrelated fixed desktop-level image, not the driven browser tab's actual content. This was independently verified by inspecting file size/dimensions before committing anything. Because of this, no PNG artifact could be honestly committed under docs/evidence/DRIFT-IV-BASE-00/ claiming to show a specific scene. Every scene and fallback listed here was instead visually reviewed live, inline, in this session (each screenshot rendered correctly and distinctly — different terrain, HUD text and landmark geometry per zone) before this report was written.

No Chrome DevTools Protocol tool (Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride / setTouchEmulationEnabled) was available in this session. The mobile structural check therefore used the project's own preview-browser resize tool, which does genuinely alter window.innerWidth/innerHeight and trigger real CSS media queries, but cannot override devicePixelRatio or emulate touch input.

requestAnimationFrame-driven continuous sampling is throttled to near-zero in every automated browser session available (document.visibilityState remains 'hidden' regardless of focus, click, or JS-level visibility overrides — confirmed empirically with an instrumented rAF counter that logged 1 frame in 33+ seconds). Only the single real-foreground mobile sample adopted in this report (Foolfoule, 50.5 fps) escaped this throttling.
